text: The runbook answers how the system works. This lesson answers a narrower, more urgent question for Priya: when do we switch, and what happens if it goes wrong.

Priya needs four things, in order. What's actually ready -- the end-to-end checklist has passed, not just been configured. The cutover mechanism -- updating DNS to point at vm-catalog01 instead of the on-prem server, with a short TTL set in advance so the change propagates quickly. The rollback trigger -- a concrete, pre-agreed condition, decided calmly now, not invented while customers are already seeing errors. And who's doing what -- the actual go-live time, who's watching dashboards, how Priya gets notified once it's stable.

The headline comes first, in the first thirty seconds: the migration is tested and ready, here's the exact cutover date and time, here's exactly what 'wrong' means and what happens if it is. Priya can ask about anything underneath that, but she should never have to wait to hear the actual ask.

If Priya asks about something genuinely out of scope -- like an Azure outage during the cutover window itself -- the honest answer is to say so plainly. A stakeholder trusts 'that's out of scope, here's why' far more than a confident-sounding guess.

With the plan presented and approved, the actual cutover happens outside this course's lessons -- the real work from here is executing exactly what was agreed, watching the dashboards, and being ready to use the rollback trigger if it's needed.
Next lesson wraps up the whole project -- what Theo actually built, the real skills underneath the Azure commands, and where Driftwood's cloud needs go from here.
